autonomic_tachycardia_diaphoresis.title: Urgent Autonomic Stress / Acute Tachycardia with Cold Sweats
autonomic_tachycardia_diaphoresis.plain_summary: Heart rate sharply above personal resting baseline combined with cold sweats, clammy skin, dizziness, or chest discomfort signals acute autonomic stress, severe volume depletion, or potential cardiovascular distress.
trigger_vitals_and_symptoms: Resting heart rate >= 120 bpm or +45 bpm above personal baseline
Dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, or chest tightness
immediate_actions: Stop exertion immediately and rest seated or lying flat.
Drink Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) slowly in 500 mL water if alert and without vomiting.
Avoid Ibuprofen/NSAIDs while orthostatic or potentially dehydrated.
Measure blood pressure and re-check heart rate after 10 to 15 minutes.
Alert Crew Medical Officer / Flight Surgeon urgently if chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting, or confusion occurs.

sources.citation: Mayo Clinic — Dehydration, Orthostatic Hypotension & Tachycardia Emergency Signs
MedlinePlus — Cold Sweats, Rapid Heart Rate & Chest Pain Urgent Evaluation

dehydration_orthostatic.title: Dehydration & Orthostatic Intolerance
dehydration_orthostatic.plain_summary: Low fluid volume reduces blood pressure when upright and triggers a fast compensatory heart rate (tachycardia), dizziness, headache, and fatigue.
trigger_vitals_and_symptoms: Elevated resting heart rate above baseline
Dizziness when standing or changing position
Low daily fluid intake or thirst
immediate_actions: Rehydrate with Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS) mixed in 500 mL potable water.
Change posture slowly and avoid sudden standing.
Avoid Ibuprofen/NSAIDs until fluid balance and kidney perfusion recover.

sources.citation: Mayo Clinic — Dehydration & Blood Pressure Regulation
NASA-STD-3001 / ISS Fluid Shift & Post-EVA Rehydration Protocol

febrile_infectious_illness.title: Fever / Possible Infection
febrile_infectious_illness.plain_summary: Elevated temperature (>= 38.0 C) alongside tachycardia, headache, or malaise requires antipyretic stabilization and serial vital tracking.
immediate_actions: Use Acetaminophen 500 mg (gentle on stomach if hydration is low; do not exceed 3,000 mg/24h).
Re-check temperature every 4 hours and monitor fluids.
Notify Flight Surgeon if fever >= 38.5 C persists past 24 hours.

sources.citation: MedlinePlus — Acetaminophen Drug Information (Fever & Pain Relief)
NASA-STD-3001 / ISS In-Flight Medical Checklist — Antipyretic Screening

cephalad_tension_headache.title: Tension / Space Fluid-Shift Headache
cephalad_tension_headache.plain_summary: Headache without fever in microgravity frequently stems from cephalad fluid shift, muscle strain, dehydration, or sleep restriction.
immediate_actions: For mild headache: rest and hydrate with water first to conserve onboard supplies.
For bothersome headache: use Acetaminophen 500 mg (preferred when hydration is uncertain) or Ibuprofen 400 mg only with food and full hydration.

sources.citation: MedlinePlus — Acetaminophen & Ibuprofen Analgesic Indications & Warnings
Wotring, V. E. (2015) · ISS Crew Medication Analysis (PMC4621588)

space_motion_vestibular.title: Space Motion Sickness (SMS) / Vestibular Discomfort
space_motion_vestibular.plain_summary: Dizziness, vertigo, or nausea worsened by head movement or floating turns indicates vestibular sensory mismatch.
trigger_vitals_and_symptoms: Dizziness or nausea triggered by head movement
immediate_actions: Stabilize head motion briefly and maintain gentle hydration.
Meclizine 25 mg treats vestibular dizziness (caution: causes drowsiness before safety-critical duties); Ondansetron 8 mg ODT provides non-sedating nausea relief.

sources.citation: MedlinePlus — Meclizine & Ondansetron Motion Sickness / Nausea Guidance
ISS Oral Medication Pack · Space Motion Sickness Protocol

circadian_sleep_deficit.title: Circadian Sleep Deficit / Fatigue
circadian_sleep_deficit.plain_summary: Shortened or fragmented sleep cycles elevate daytime tiredness, headache risk, and mild autonomic stress.
immediate_actions: Keep a dark, quiet sleep station and stop stimulants before rest period.
If bothersome across multiple cycles, low-dose Melatonin 3 mg 30 to 60 minutes before scheduled sleep helps re-align circadian rhythm.

sources.citation: MedlinePlus — Melatonin Adult Dosing (0.5–5 mg) & Safety Precautions
NASA Circadian Entrainment & Sleep Support Protocol

post_exercise_tachycardia.title: Post-Exercise Heart Rate Recovery
post_exercise_tachycardia.plain_summary: Elevated heart rate within 45 minutes of ARED or cardiovascular exercise without headache, fever, dizziness, or cold sweats represents normal cardiovascular recovery.
trigger_vitals_and_symptoms: Elevated heart rate right after workout
No fever, dizziness, nausea, or cold sweats
immediate_actions: Rest 15 to 20 minutes and drink water.
No medication is needed; re-check heart rate after cooldown.

sources.citation: NASA Countermeasure ARED Recovery & Hydration Guidance

sans_ocular_shift.title: Ocular / Visual Fluid-Shift Check (SANS)
sans_ocular_shift.plain_summary: New visual acuity changes in microgravity (especially with cephalad fluid fullness or headache) can signal Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) from headward fluid shift and intracranial pressure changes.
trigger_vitals_and_symptoms: Visual acuity change (near-vision blur or focus shift)
Cephalad fluid fullness or headache in microgravity
immediate_actions: Schedule ocular Amsler grid / ultrasound optic-nerve check and alert the Flight Surgeon / CMO.
Avoid routine NSAIDs; use Acetaminophen 500 mg only if accompanying headache is bothersome.

sources.citation: Mader et al. (2011) · Ophthalmology — Microgravity Optic Disc & Visual Shifts (PMID 21840600)
NASA Human Research Program — Risk of Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS)

musculoskeletal_strain.title: Musculoskeletal / ARED Strain
musculoskeletal_strain.plain_summary: Localized muscle discomfort or soreness without fever or systemic dehydration typically follows resistance exercise (ARED) or EVA suit load.
trigger_vitals_and_symptoms: Normal body temperature without systemic illness
immediate_actions: Rest the strained muscle group and hydrate adequately; take Ibuprofen 400 mg only with food and full hydration (or use Acetaminophen 500 mg if hydration is uncertain).

sources.citation: MedlinePlus / NIH — Ibuprofen Drug Information (Pain & Inflammation)
Eyal et al. (2019) · Spaceflight Analgesic & NSAID Precautions (PMID 31152244)

nausea_gi_support.title: Acute Nausea / Gastrointestinal Discomfort
nausea_gi_support.plain_summary: Isolated or persistent nausea without fever requires a non-sedating anti-emetic that dissolves orally without requiring large fluid boluses.
immediate_actions: Take Ondansetron 8 mg ODT (dissolves on tongue without water) and sip Oral Rehydration Salts slowly once stomach settles.

sources.citation: MedlinePlus / NIH — Ondansetron ODT Drug Information
Wotring, V. E. (2015) · ISS Crew Anti-Emetic Usage (PMC4621588)
